title: An act to amend the Fair Minimum Wage Act of 2007 to reduce a scheduled increase in the minimum wage applicable to American Samoa.
sponsor: Del. Radewagen, Aumua Amata Coleman [R-AS-At Large]
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the Senate on September 30, 2015. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

(Sec. 1) This Act amends the Fair Minimum Wage Act of 2007 to prescribe a $0.40 per hour incremental increase in the transitional minimum wage for each American Samoa industry, beginning on September 30, 2015, and on September 30 triennially until the minimum wage applicable to American Samoa is equal to the minimum wage for the United States.

The deadline for the Government Accountability Office (GAO) report assessing the impact of minimum wage increases in American Samoa is changed from September 1, 2011, to April 1, 2017, with a subsequent report due by April 1, 2020.

The GAO shall also report on alternative ways of increasing the minimum wage in American Samoa to keep pace with the cost of living there and eventually equal the minimum wage for the United States.

This Act, and the amendments made by it, shall take effect as of September 29, 2015.

summary.headline: This law slows the scheduled minimum wage increases for American Samoa and moves some federal report deadlines.
summary.what_it_does: It changes the Fair Minimum Wage Act of 2007 so that the wage for each American Samoa industry rises by 40 cents per hour, instead of a larger scheduled amount. Increases happen every three years, starting September 30, 2015, until the territory's minimum wage matches the U.S. minimum wage. The law also pushes back the deadline for a Government Accountability Office report on minimum wage effects in American Samoa to April 1, 2017, with another report due by April 1, 2020. That report must also look at other ways to raise the territory's wage to keep up with local living costs.

who_it_affects.how: Their minimum wage rises by smaller, less frequent steps than the earlier schedule set, so the timing of future raises changes.
They must pay the new, slower-rising minimum wage schedule for each industry.
It must complete reports on American Samoa's minimum wage by new deadlines and study alternative wage-increase methods.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Retroactively as of September 29, 2015, with the first 40-cent increase beginning September 30, 2015.
